summary: Unlinks node a2 from a doubly linked list owned by this. Walks from the list head at this+0x14 following node next pointers (node+100) until a2 or the end of the list is found. If a2 has a previous node (node+104), that node's next pointer is set to a2's next; otherwise the head at this+0x14 is replaced by a2's next. If a2 has a next node, that node's previous pointer (node+104) is set to a2's previous; otherwise the tail at this+0x18 is replaced by a2's previous.

operations.description: NULL target node a2 causes an immediate return; nothing is unlinked.
Start traversal at the list head stored at this+0x14.
Empty list (head at this+0x14 is NULL) skips the traversal and returns without unlinking.
Walk nodes by following each node's next pointer at node+100 until the current node equals the target a2.
If the walk reaches a NULL next pointer before finding a2, the target is not in the list and the function returns without unlinking.
Read the target node's previous pointer stored at a2+104.
Branch on whether the target has a previous node.
Target has a previous node: set that previous node's next pointer (node+100) to the target's next pointer, splicing the target out.
Target has no previous node and is the head: replace the head at this+0x14 with the target's next pointer.
Read the target node's next pointer stored at a2+100.
Branch on whether the target has a next node.
Target has a next node: set that next node's previous pointer (node+104) to the target's previous pointer.
Target has no next node and is the tail: replace the tail at this+0x18 with the target's previous pointer.
